question: Does R129 CUTLASS supply exact, in-gate kernels for the larger-K production shapes that failed the oneDNN catalog, enabling a heterogeneous shape map with pinned oneDNN M32 for K3072/N5120?

basis.candidate_rule: Use pinned oneDNN source-M32 for the duplicated K3072/N5120 shape. Screen R129 CUTLASS M16-small/M32-direct on all shapes, selecting it only where it clears the unchanged identity, numerical, and latency gates.

gates.cutlass_identity_and_numerical: Every shape must retain one row-0 class, exact M512 prefixes, exact M200 permutation/repeat, exact M168 random appended-row content, finite output, and max absolute error versus oneDNN <=0.06.
gates.cutlass_latency_for_selection: A shape may select CUTLASS only if geometric-mean candidate/oneDNN <=1.15 and no timed M >1.50x. Duplicated K,N shapes must select the same mechanism.
gates.catalog_progress: K5120/N8192, K5120/N7168, K5120/N17408, and K8704/N5120 must all have a passing CUTLASS candidate. K3072/N5120 remains assigned to pinned oneDNN M32 and must be revalidated in the eventual integrated binary because R124's two labels straddled the worst-point gate under timing drift.
gates.on_pass: Implement one narrow binary containing both mechanisms, then rerun all-six identity and latency plus a call-count-weighted <=3% decode-step overhead model before any server.
gates.on_failure: Preserve the result. Optimize only the specific failing K/N tile family; do not launch a server.
gates.health: No new Xe fault, reset, timeout, hang, coredump, or device loss.
